what_worked: Clear power-law thesis with well-chosen median-vs-mean contrast and honest zero-revenue caveat.
fix_next: The deck is too thin at four slides—add category, provider, or anonymity analysis to substantiate the concentration thesis beyond top-line deciles.
verdict: Focused and honest but too narrow to be truly insightful.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: Title says 83.7% in top 10% of startups—the frozen reference gives top-10 companies (not top decile) at 49.6%; 83.7% for top decile is unverified and likely conflates decile with top-10. Slide 2: Mean stated as $15,596—actual mean is $15,596,344.59/1000 ≈ $15,596, which is correct, but the median of $400 is not verifiable from the reference (overall median not provided). Slide 2: 21.6% zero-revenue—actual is 216/1000 = 21.6%, correct. Slide 3: Top-10 revenue sum ($2,845K+$985K+$868K+$858K+$575K+$391K+$386K+$365K+$242K+$222K = ~$7,737K) yields 49.6% of $15.6M, which checks out, but the claim that Stan alone earns more than #2–#6 combined ($985+$868+$858+$575+$391 = $3,677K vs $2,845K) is false.

evidence.insight: Slide 2 decile chart and median-vs-mean comparison are the core insight; slide 4 offers practical takeaways but stays generic. No category or segment-level analysis.
evidence.narrative: Slides flow logically: market shape → whales → implications. Coherent but brief; the 'so what' on slide 4 is reasonable but could be sharper with data backing.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets dataset, n, and date. No discussion of missingness (274 missing category, 241 missing country) or selection bias. Audience implied but not stated.
evidence.accuracy: 83.7% top-decile claim is unverified against reference. Stan vs #2–#6 comparison appears arithmetically wrong. Mean $15,596 is correct. 21.6% zero-revenue correct. 49.6% top-10 share correct.
evidence.visual: Clean, restrained design with consistent typography and color. Decile bar chart is effective. Slide 4 uses decorative colored squares that add nothing. Good legibility throughout.
evidence.ai_slop: Slide 4 decorative squares are mildly sloppy template artifacts; otherwise minimal slop.
